description: Users can sign in using a third-party identity provider.
steps: Navigate to the application while unauthenticated.
Verify the login page is displayed with a sign-in button.
Click the sign-in button.
Complete the authentication flow.
Verify the user is redirected to the notebook page after successful sign-in.

description: Users can sign out, which clears the session and returns them to the login page.
steps: Sign in as an authenticated user.
Click the profile avatar button in the header.
Click the 'Sign Out' button in the popover.
Verify the session is cleared.
Verify the user is returned to the login page.

description: Unauthenticated users are redirected to the login page when accessing any protected route.
steps: Attempt to navigate to the notebook page while unauthenticated.
Verify the user is redirected to the login page.
Verify that after signing in, the user is taken to the originally requested page.

description: Authenticated users are redirected away from the login page to their original intended destination or the home page.
steps: Sign in as an authenticated user.
Navigate to the login page.
Verify the user is redirected to the home page (or the previously intended page if available).

description: A loading state is displayed while the application determines the user's authentication status.
steps: Navigate to the application.
Verify a loading indicator is displayed while authentication is being determined.
Verify the appropriate page renders once the user's status is known.

description: Authentication state persists across page refreshes (session persistence).
steps: Sign in as an authenticated user.
Refresh the page.
Verify the user remains authenticated without needing to sign in again.
Verify the user is taken directly to the notebook (not the login page).

description: The login page provides a toggle to switch between sign-in and sign-up modes.
steps: Navigate to the login page.
Verify the sign-in form is displayed by default.
Verify there is a visible control to switch to sign-up mode.
Switch to sign-up mode.
Verify the sign-up form is displayed with fields for email, password, and password confirmation.
Verify there is a visible control to switch back to sign-in mode.
Switch back to sign-in mode.
Verify the sign-in form is displayed again.

description: Users can create a new account by providing an email address and a password with confirmation. After successful sign-up, the user is automatically signed in and redirected to the home page.
steps: Navigate to the login page and switch to sign-up mode.
Enter a valid email address.
Enter a password and matching confirmation.
Submit the sign-up form.
Verify the account is created successfully.
Verify the user is automatically signed in.
Verify the user is redirected to the home page.

description: Sign-up displays appropriate error messages when the input is invalid, such as mismatched passwords or a duplicate email address.
steps: Switch to sign-up mode on the login page.
Enter a password and a non-matching confirmation.
Attempt to submit the form.
Verify an error is displayed indicating the passwords do not match.
Correct the confirmation to match the password.
Enter an email address that is already registered.
Attempt to submit the form.
Verify an error is displayed indicating the account already exists.

description: The system supports three roles: 'user', 'author', and 'admin'.
steps: Verify that users can be assigned the roles 'user', 'author', and 'admin'.
Verify that no other role values are accepted by the system.

description: New users receive only the 'user' role by default upon account creation.
steps: Create a new user account.
Verify the user has only the 'user' role.
Verify the user does not have 'author' or 'admin' roles.

description: A pre-configured bootstrap admin receives all three roles ('user', 'author', 'admin') on first sign-up.
steps: Configure the application with a designated admin email.
Create a new account using that email.
Verify the user has the 'user', 'author', and 'admin' roles.

description: The notebook route requires the 'author' role. Users without it are redirected to the lobby.
steps: Sign in as a user with only the 'user' role (no 'author' role).
Attempt to navigate to the notebook page.
Verify the user is redirected to the lobby page.

description: The admin route requires the 'admin' role. Users without it are redirected to the home page.
steps: Sign in as a user without the 'admin' role.
Attempt to navigate to the admin page.
Verify the user is redirected to the home page.

description: The admin panel link in the header is only visible to users with the 'admin' role on desktop viewports.
steps: Sign in as a user with the 'admin' role on a desktop viewport.
Verify the settings icon (admin link) is visible in the header.
Sign in as a user without the 'admin' role.
Verify the settings icon is not visible in the header.

description: The admin panel link is not visible on mobile viewports even for admin users.
steps: Sign in as a user with the 'admin' role on a mobile viewport.
Verify the admin link is not visible in the header.

description: Privileged operations (toggling roles, listing users) verify the caller has the 'admin' role before executing.
steps: Attempt to toggle a user's role without admin privileges.
Verify the request is rejected with an appropriate error.
Attempt to toggle a user's role with admin privileges.
Verify the request succeeds.

description: Any authenticated user can create notes.
steps: Sign in as an authenticated user.
Create a new note.
Verify the note is created successfully in the database.

description: Users can only read their own notes (where the note's author field matches the user's ID).
steps: Sign in as User A and create a note.
Sign in as User B.
Attempt to read User A's note.
Verify the read is denied with a permission error.

description: Users can only update their own notes.
steps: Sign in as User A and create a note.
Sign in as User B.
Attempt to update User A's note.
Verify the update is denied with a permission error.

description: Users can only delete their own notes.
steps: Sign in as User A and create a note.
Sign in as User B.
Attempt to delete User A's note.
Verify the delete is denied with a permission error.

description: Users can only read and write their own settings.
steps: Sign in as User A and save a theme preference.
Sign in as User B.
Attempt to read User A's settings.
Verify the read is denied.
Attempt to update User A's settings.
Verify the update is denied.

description: Any authenticated user can create their own settings document.
steps: Sign in as a new user with no existing settings.
Save a theme preference.
Verify the settings document is created successfully.

description: Admins can read all user records. Non-admin users can only read their own user record.
steps: Sign in as an admin user.
Request all user records.
Verify all records are returned.
Sign in as a non-admin user.
Attempt to read another user's record.
Verify the read is denied.

description: Only admins can update user records (for role changes).
steps: Sign in as a non-admin user.
Attempt to update any user record.
Verify the update is denied.
Sign in as an admin user.
Update a user record.
Verify the update succeeds.

description: Unauthenticated requests to protected resources are rejected with appropriate errors.
steps: Attempt to read notes without authentication.
Verify the request is rejected.
Attempt to perform a privileged operation without authentication.
Verify the request is rejected with an 'unauthenticated' error.

description: Unauthorized requests receive permission-denied errors.
steps: Sign in as a non-admin user.
Attempt to perform an admin-only operation (e.g., toggle a role).
Verify the request is rejected with a 'permission-denied' error code.

description: Admins can read all role-update notifications. Non-admin users can only read their own role-update notifications.
steps: Sign in as an admin user.
Read the global role-update notification.
Verify the read succeeds.
Sign in as a non-admin user.
Attempt to read the global role-update notification.
Verify the read is denied.
Verify the user can read their own role-update notification.

description: When a new user account is created, the system automatically assigns initial roles and persists the user profile.
steps: Create a new user account via sign-up.
Verify the user is assigned the 'user' role.
Verify the user's profile is persisted and retrievable.

description: The lobby page displays a 'Your application is being reviewed!' message for users who only have the 'user' role (no 'author' role).
steps: Sign in as a user with only the 'user' role.
Navigate to the lobby page.
Verify the page displays 'Your application is being reviewed!'.
Verify the page displays 'Come back soon to check if it has been approved.'.

description: The lobby automatically redirects users who have the 'author' role to the notebook page.
steps: Sign in as a user with the 'author' role.
Navigate to the lobby page.
Verify the user is redirected to the notebook page.

description: The lobby automatically redirects users who have the 'admin' role (but not 'author') to the admin page.
steps: Sign in as a user with the 'admin' role but not the 'author' role.
Navigate to the lobby page.
Verify the user is redirected to the admin page.

description: Users can create a new empty note. The note is assigned a unique ID and associated with the creating user.
steps: Sign in as an author.
Click the create note button in the notebook toolbar.
Verify a new note appears in the notes list.
Verify the note has a unique ID.
Verify the note is associated with the current user.
Verify the note content is empty.
Verify the note has an initial version number.

description: A note's display title is derived from the first line of its content. If the content is empty or the first line is blank, the title falls back to 'untitled'.
steps: Create a new empty note.
Verify the note's displayed title is 'untitled'.
Type 'My First Note' as the first line.
Verify the displayed title updates to 'My First Note'.
Add a second line of text.
Verify the title still shows only the first line.
Clear all content.
Verify the title reverts to 'untitled'.

description: Users can edit note content in a plain text editor. Changes are reflected immediately in the local state.
steps: Open a note in the editor.
Type text into the editor.
Verify the text appears immediately.
Verify the note's title in the toolbar updates based on the first line.
Verify the editor supports multi-line text input.

description: Note changes are auto-saved to the server after a short idle period.
steps: Open a note and type text.
Stop typing and wait briefly.
Verify the changes are persisted to the server.
Verify the note's updated timestamp is refreshed.
Verify the note's version is incremented.

description: Users can delete a note. Deleting an open note closes the editor.
steps: Create a note and open it in the editor.
Click the delete button on the note.
Verify the note is removed from the notes list.
Verify the editor is closed (no note displayed).
Verify the note is deleted from the server.

description: Users can duplicate a note. The duplicate has 'copy of [title]' prepended to the original content, gets a new unique ID, and opens automatically in the editor.
steps: Create a note with content 'Hello World'.
Click the duplicate button.
Verify a new note is created in the notes list.
Verify the new note's content is 'copy of Hello World\nHello World'.
Verify the new note has a different ID from the original.
Verify the new note is automatically opened in the editor.

description: The notes list displays each note as a card showing: title, created date, and updated date.
steps: Create multiple notes with different content.
Verify each note card in the list shows the derived title.
Verify each note card shows a 'Created [date]' label.
Verify each note card shows an 'Updated [date]' label.
Verify dates are formatted in a human-readable format.

description: Each note tracks its content, author, version, and timestamps for creation and last update.
steps: Create a note and save it.
Verify the note record contains: content, author, version, creation timestamp, and last-update timestamp.
Verify the creation timestamp is set on first save.
Verify the last-update timestamp is updated on subsequent saves.
Verify the version increments on each save.

description: The creation timestamp is set on the first save. The last-update timestamp is set on every save.
steps: Create a new note.
Save the note.
Verify the creation timestamp is set.
Verify the last-update timestamp is set.
Save the note again.
Verify the creation timestamp remains unchanged.
Verify the last-update timestamp is updated.

description: Creating a note automatically opens it in the currently selected editor.
steps: Verify no note is open in the editor.
Click the create note button.
Verify the newly created note is displayed in the editor.
Verify the editor textarea has focus.

description: Each note card in the list has duplicate and delete action buttons.
steps: Create a note.
Verify the note card in the list shows a duplicate button.
Verify the note card in the list shows a delete button.

description: When both editors show the same note and that note is deleted, the notebook resets to default state (no notes open).
steps: Open a note in the main editor.
Send the same note to the additional editor (desktop only).
Delete the note.
Verify both editors are closed.
Verify the notebook state is reset to default.

description: When the main editor's note is deleted and the additional editor has a different note, the additional editor's note moves to the main editor.
steps: Open note A in the main editor (desktop).
Open note B in the additional editor.
Delete note A.
Verify note B is now displayed in the main editor.
Verify the additional editor is closed.

description: Notes can be sorted by created date, newest first. This is the default sort order.
steps: Create three notes at different times.
Verify the notes list displays them in newest-first order by default.
Open the sort menu.
Verify 'by created date (newest first)' is highlighted as the current selection.

description: Notes can be sorted by created date, oldest first.
steps: Create three notes at different times.
Open the sort menu.
Select 'by created date (oldest first)'.
Verify the notes list reorders to show oldest notes first.

description: Notes can be sorted by title alphabetically (A to Z).
steps: Create notes with titles starting with 'C', 'A', and 'B' (first line of content).
Open the sort menu.
Select 'by title (ABC...)'.
Verify the notes list reorders to show A, B, C.

description: Notes can be sorted by title in reverse alphabetical order (Z to A).
steps: Create notes with titles starting with 'C', 'A', and 'B'.
Open the sort menu.
Select 'by title (ZYX...)'.
Verify the notes list reorders to show C, B, A.

description: The selected sort order persists during the session (but resets to default on page reload).
steps: Select 'by title (ABC...)' sort order.
Navigate away from the notebook and back.
Verify the sort order is still 'by title (ABC...)'.
Reload the page.
Verify the sort order resets to 'by created date (newest first)'.

description: The editor is an accessible plain-text editing area that fills the available space.
steps: Open a note in the editor.
Verify the editor is a plain-text editing area.
Verify the editor fills the available width and height.
Verify the editor does not allow resizing.
Verify the editor is accessible (has an appropriate accessible name).

description: The editor toolbar displays the note's derived title.
steps: Open a note with content 'My Title' on the first line.
Verify the toolbar shows 'My Title'.
Change the first line to 'New Title'.
Verify the toolbar updates to show 'New Title'.

description: The editor toolbar has a duplicate button. On desktop, the main editor toolbar also has a 'send to additional editor' button, and the additional editor toolbar has a close button.
steps: Open a note in the main editor on desktop.
Verify the toolbar shows a duplicate button.
Verify the toolbar shows a 'send to additional editor' button.
Open the additional editor.
Verify the additional editor toolbar shows a duplicate button and a close button.
On mobile, verify only the duplicate and close buttons are shown (no split button).

description: Clicking a note in the list opens it in the currently selected editor.
steps: Create multiple notes.
Click on note A in the list.
Verify note A is displayed in the active editor.
Click on note B in the list.
Verify note B replaces note A in the active editor.

description: The currently open note is visually highlighted in the notes list.
steps: Create multiple notes.
Open note A in the editor.
Verify note A's card in the list has a selected/highlighted background.
Verify other note cards do not have the highlighted background.
Open note B.
Verify note B is now highlighted and note A is no longer highlighted.

description: The currently focused editor has a visual indicator distinguishing it from inactive editors.
steps: Open a note in the main editor on desktop.
Verify the main editor has a visual focus indicator.
Open the additional editor with a different note.
Click on the additional editor.
Verify the additional editor now has the focus indicator.
Verify the main editor's focus indicator is removed.

description: When a note is opened in the editor, the textarea receives focus with the cursor positioned at the end of the content.
steps: Create a note with some text content.
Click the note in the list to open it.
Verify the textarea has focus.
Verify the cursor is positioned at the end of the text.

description: On desktop, clicking the 'send to additional editor' button opens a split view with two editors side by side (50%/50%).
steps: Open a note in the main editor on desktop.
Click the 'send to additional editor' button.
Verify the additional editor opens alongside the main editor.
Verify both editors share the available width equally (50/50).
Verify the note is displayed in the additional editor.

description: Each editor in the split view can display a different note independently.
steps: Open note A in the main editor.
Send note A to the additional editor.
Click on note B in the notes list (while main editor is selected).
Verify note B is displayed in the main editor.
Verify note A remains displayed in the additional editor.

description: Clicking a note in the list opens it in whichever editor is currently selected (focused).
steps: Open the split view with two editors on desktop.
Click on the additional editor to select it.
Click on a note in the list.
Verify the note opens in the additional editor (not the main).
Click on the main editor to select it.
Click on a different note.
Verify that note opens in the main editor.

description: The additional editor has a close button that returns the view to a single editor and selects the main editor.
steps: Open the split view on desktop.
Click the close button on the additional editor.
Verify the additional editor is closed.
Verify only the main editor remains visible.
Verify the main editor is selected.

description: The split editor automatically closes when the viewport shrinks to mobile or tablet size.
steps: Open the split view on a desktop viewport.
Resize the browser window to a tablet-sized viewport.
Verify the additional editor is automatically closed.
Verify only the main editor remains.

description: When the main editor's note is closed (via deletion), the additional editor's note moves to the main editor position.
steps: Open note A in the main editor and note B in the additional editor.
Delete note A.
Verify note B moves to the main editor.
Verify the additional editor is closed.

description: The admin panel is accessible via the settings icon in the header. It is only visible to admin users on desktop viewports.
steps: Sign in as an admin user on a desktop viewport.
Click the settings icon in the header.
Verify the admin panel is displayed.
Verify the admin page loads the admin table.

description: The admin panel displays a table of all users with columns: Email, Author (checkbox), Admin (checkbox), Created, Signed In, User UID.
steps: Navigate to the admin panel as an admin user.
Verify the table has columns: Email, Author, Admin, Created, Signed In, User UID.
Verify all registered users appear in the table.
Verify the Author and Admin columns show checkboxes.

description: Admins can toggle the 'author' role for any user via the checkbox in the admin table.
steps: Navigate to the admin panel.
Find a user without the 'author' role.
Check the Author checkbox for that user.
Verify the role change is sent to the server.
Verify the user now has the 'author' role.
Uncheck the Author checkbox.
Verify the 'author' role is revoked.

description: Admins can toggle the 'admin' role for any user via the checkbox in the admin table.
steps: Navigate to the admin panel.
Find a user without the 'admin' role.
Check the Admin checkbox for that user.
Verify the role change is sent to the server.
Verify the user now has the 'admin' role.
Uncheck the Admin checkbox.
Verify the 'admin' role is revoked.

description: Role changes in the admin panel are executed server-side with admin verification.
steps: Toggle a role in the admin panel.
Verify the role change is processed server-side.
Verify the system confirms the caller has admin privileges before applying the change.
Verify the role change is applied to the target user.
Verify the user's persisted profile reflects the new roles.

description: The admin route is not available on mobile viewports.
steps: View the application on a mobile viewport.
Attempt to navigate to the admin page.
Verify the user is redirected away from the admin page.

description: Non-admin users who attempt to access the admin route on desktop are redirected to the home page.
steps: Sign in as a non-admin user on desktop.
Navigate to the admin page.
Verify the user is redirected to the home page.

description: The header displays a profile button showing the user's avatar.
steps: Sign in as an authenticated user.
Verify the header shows a clickable avatar button.
Verify the avatar shows the user's profile photo (or a default avatar).

description: Clicking the profile button opens a popover displaying: avatar, display name, email, and user ID.
steps: Click the profile avatar button.
Verify a popover opens below the avatar.
Verify the popover shows a larger avatar image.
Verify the popover shows the user's display name.
Verify the popover shows the user's email.
Verify the popover shows the user's ID.

description: The profile popover includes a 'Sign Out' button.
steps: Open the profile popover.
Verify a 'Sign Out' button is displayed.
Click 'Sign Out'.
Verify the user is signed out and the page reloads.

description: The header includes a light/dark theme toggle switch with sun and moon icons.
steps: Sign in as an authenticated user.
Verify the header displays a theme toggle switch.
Verify the switch shows a sun icon (light mode) or moon icon (dark mode).
Toggle the switch.
Verify the entire application theme changes between light and dark mode.

description: The theme preference is persisted to the server per user.
steps: Toggle the theme to dark mode.
Verify the theme preference is saved to the user's settings on the server.
Sign out and sign back in.
Verify dark mode is restored from the server.
Sign in as a different user.
Verify the other user has their own independent theme preference.

description: The theme is loaded from the server on application initialization.
steps: Set the theme to dark mode and ensure it is saved.
Reload the page.
Verify dark mode is applied after the app initializes.
Verify there is no visible flash of the wrong theme.

description: If no saved theme preference exists, the default theme (light) is applied.
steps: Sign in as a new user with no saved settings.
Verify the application uses light mode by default.

description: Mobile layout is used on small viewports.
steps: Set the viewport to a mobile width.
Verify the mobile layout is rendered (notes list as main view, drawer for editor).

description: Header icons are visually reduced at tablet sizes.
steps: Set the viewport to a tablet width.
Verify header icons are visually smaller than at desktop size.

description: Desktop layout is used on large viewports.
steps: Set the viewport to a desktop width.
Verify the desktop layout is rendered with a multi-pane layout.

description: Desktop layout has a sidebar with a toolbar and notes list, and an editor area that fills the remaining space.
steps: View the application on a desktop viewport.
Verify there is a narrower sidebar column containing a toolbar and notes list.
Verify the editor fills the remaining horizontal space.

description: Mobile layout shows notes list as the main view. Tapping a note opens the editor in a right-side drawer that covers the full viewport.
steps: View the application on a mobile viewport.
Verify the notes list is the main view.
Tap on a note in the list.
Verify a drawer slides in from the right showing the editor.
Verify the drawer covers the full viewport width and height.
Verify the mobile editor has a close button.
Click the close button.
Verify the drawer closes and the notes list is visible again.

description: The mobile platform does not include an admin route.
steps: View the application on a mobile viewport.
Verify no admin route is accessible.
Verify no admin link is visible in the header.

description: The mobile platform does not support split editor functionality.
steps: View the application on a mobile viewport.
Open a note in the editor.
Verify there is no 'send to additional editor' button.
Verify only the duplicate and close buttons are in the toolbar.

description: The application switches between desktop and mobile layouts based on viewport width.
steps: Set viewport to a desktop width.
Verify the desktop layout is rendered.
Resize to a mobile width.
Verify the mobile layout is rendered.
Resize back to desktop width.
Verify the desktop layout is rendered again.

description: Notes sync in real-time across clients. Changes made in one client appear in another without a page refresh.
steps: Sign in as the same user in two browser windows.
Create a note in window A.
Verify the note appears in window B's notes list without refreshing.
Edit the note in window A.
Verify the changes appear in window B.

description: Local edits are applied optimistically. The user sees their changes immediately without waiting for server confirmation.
steps: Open a note in the editor.
Type text.
Verify the text appears instantly in the editor (no delay).
Verify the local state is updated before the server write completes.

description: Concurrent edits from multiple clients are resolved without data loss.
steps: Open the same note in two browser windows.
Make different edits in both windows simultaneously.
Verify the edits are merged without errors.
Verify one consistent version of the note is established across both clients.
Verify no data is silently lost.

description: The notes collection updates in real-time. New notes appear and deleted notes disappear in all connected clients.
steps: Sign in as the same user in two browser windows.
Create a note in window A.
Verify the note appears in window B's list.
Delete the note in window A.
Verify the note disappears from window B's list.

description: The application is installable as a PWA with a manifest that includes name, icons, and standalone display mode.
steps: Navigate to the application.
Verify the web manifest is loaded with name 'Quiet Notes'.
Verify the manifest specifies 'standalone' display mode.
Verify the manifest includes icons at standard PWA sizes.
Verify the manifest includes a maskable icon.
Verify the browser offers to install the application.

description: A service worker caches the app shell for offline loading.
steps: Load the application and wait for the service worker to install.
Verify static assets (HTML, CSS, JS, icons) are cached.
Go offline.
Verify the app shell loads from the cache.

description: When a new version is detected, a non-blocking snackbar appears with the message 'New version available' and an 'Update' button.
steps: Deploy a new version of the application.
Verify a snackbar appears at the bottom-right of the screen.
Verify the snackbar message says 'New version available'.
Verify the snackbar includes an 'Update' button.
Verify the snackbar does not block user interaction with the app.

description: Clicking the 'Update' button in the version prompt refreshes the application to load the new version.
steps: When the update snackbar is visible, click the 'Update' button.
Verify the service worker is updated.
Verify the page reloads with the new version.

description: The application provides Apple touch icons for iOS devices.
steps: Verify the application includes apple-touch-icon files at standard iOS sizes.
Verify the icons are discoverable by iOS devices.

description: The logo 'Qn.' in the header is clickable and navigates to the home page.
steps: Sign in and navigate to the admin panel.
Click the 'Qn.' logo in the header.
Verify the user is navigated to the home page.

description: The header includes a GitHub icon link that opens the repository in a new tab.
steps: Verify the header displays a GitHub icon.
Click the GitHub icon.
Verify a new tab opens with the repository URL.

description: The header is always visible at the top of the page while body content scrolls independently.
steps: Sign in to the application.
Verify the header is visible at the top.
Scroll the body content.
Verify the header remains fixed at the top.
Navigate between different routes.
Verify the header persists across all authenticated routes.

description: The application fills the full viewport with no scrollable overflow on the body.
steps: Load the application.
Verify the app fills the full viewport.
Verify there is no horizontal or vertical scrollbar on the page body.

description: Unmatched routes redirect to the notebook page for authenticated users.
steps: Sign in as an author.
Navigate to the home page.
Verify the user is redirected to the notebook page.
Navigate to a non-existent page.
Verify the user is redirected to the notebook page.

description: Application errors are captured in a global error state queue and displayed to the user.
steps: Trigger an error condition (e.g., a failed server operation).
Verify the error is added to the global error state.
Verify an error dialog is displayed to the user showing the error details.

description: Permission-denied errors are handled specifically and display the error code.
steps: Trigger a permission-denied error.
Verify the error dialog displays the error name and code.
Verify the error is distinguishable from other error types.

description: Users can dismiss errors from the error dialog via an OK button.
steps: Trigger an error that displays the error dialog.
Verify the dialog has an OK button.
Click the OK button.
Verify the error is dismissed and the dialog closes.
Verify the error is removed from the error queue.

description: Fatal rendering errors are caught and displayed with a 'Fatal Error' message instead of a blank screen.
steps: Trigger a fatal rendering error.
Verify the error is caught and a 'Fatal Error' message is displayed.
Verify the application does not crash to a blank screen.
